explanation: Remember only the previous and current nodes. Their relationship tells whether traversal is descending from the parent, returning from the left subtree, or returning from the right subtree; visit the node between its two subtrees.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Every tree edge is traversed at most downward and upward; three node cursors replace a stack.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space, excluding the O(n) returned traversal. Previous/current/next cursors replace a stack; only the returned value list grows.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: The previous/current relationship identifies the traversal phase without a stack. Arriving from the parent means the left subtree remains unvisited; returning from the left means the root should now be emitted; returning from the right means the entire subtree is complete. The selected next edge is exactly the edge a recursive inorder traversal would take. Each edge is traversed only a constant number of times, and each value is emitted once.
walkthrough: For [16, 7, 25, 2, 11, null, 30], descend 16 → 7 → 2 and emit 2. Return to 7 and emit 7, then visit and emit 11. Returning through 7 reaches 16, which is emitted before the right subtree 25, 30. Return [2, 7, 11, 16, 25, 30], using only previous/current/next node references beyond the result list. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: A node without a left child is emitted on its first arrival.
Returning from a right child must climb without emitting the parent a second time.
